column3: English locale stub for the package UI: only meta.title "ptc-runtime-node", no description key.
Chinese locale stub: meta.title "Node PTC 运行时" plus a meta.description the English file lacks.
Published manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node 0.2.1-rc.2; ships lib/index.js, lib/process.js and lib/persistent-process.js (the two child bundles remote hosts run).
Heading-hash record pairing the English and Chinese Node backend READMEs; 14 hashed sections.
Package reference for the Node backend: config table, per-call vs persistent-in-memory modes, deadline semantics, failure mapping, and the stated limits.
Chinese mirror of the Node backend README (181 lines); its source-map table omits src/output-ledger.ts, which the English one lists.
Validates binding namespaces and error-class names against the seam's shared exclusion sets before a process starts, and encodes a host binding's lossless-JSON result into a reply frame.
Child-side evaluator: LogBuffer, five-method console shim, stream-write capture, lossless completion/exception preparation, binding namespaces and the AsyncFunction program invocation.
Length-prefixed JSON transport with per-frame and queued-byte caps, fatal UTF-8 decoding, corked writes and io-vs-protocol failure classification.
Schemastery config schema (executionMode, limits, launch union) plus validateConfig, which names the offending key and enforces the 32-bit frame-length ceiling.
The only environment file: the six retained native OS variables and the scrubber that empties the program-visible process.env into a null-prototype object.
The host execution loop: resolve, sandbox confinement, spawn, control-frame validation, binding dispatch, deadline/abort, output admission and the failure taxonomy.
Lossless-JSON boundary: captured-intrinsic snapshot, flat bounded-depth token encode/decode, and rejection of exotic containers, sparse arrays, cycles and foreign-realm forgeries.
Chooses the worker executable and bootstrap in the execution world; maps the source bootstrap through fs.processPathFromHostPath and refuses an unmappable or packaged-persistent launch.
Exact JSON serialized-byte accounting and code-point-aligned truncation, computed without materialising the escaped form and using module-captured intrinsics.
Combined outer-output ledger for one run: admits logs against one byte cap, then retains a fitting prefix and a fixed diagnostic on overflow.
Bounded drain of raw process output and terminate-and-drain of a managed process; a false drain becomes a worker-exit failure.
Four-line built entry for the retained REPL bundle: opens the inherited control channel and calls runPersistentMain with argv[2] as the message limit.
Child-side Node REPL serving sequential evaluations: AsyncLocalStorage attribution, replaced process object, redefined _ and _error globals, and the leading-brace workaround.
In-memory retained mode: one Kernel per stateOwner (WeakMap), per-owner concurrency refusal, the cleanupPending barrier, and policy-change refusal until release.
Tracks admitted processes against a Session and invalidates them on a sandbox/mode change; wait() blocks the next program until the previous cleanup is observed.
Four-line built entry for the per-call child bundle: opens the inherited control channel and calls runNodeMain.
Per-call child main: ready/boot handshake, program run, terminal frame flush, and a deliberate wait for the host to close the channel so a late reply is not lost.
Wire vocabulary for the control channel: call/log/output-limit/done frames plus replies; logs stream eagerly so output survives a mid-run kill.
Pins binding validation: unusable globals, reserved names, duplicate globals and injected constructors, and that a null-prototype functions object is preserved by identity.
Exercises the child evaluator in-process with the test playing the host: lossy completions, huge thrown values, typed rejections, clone failures and the LogBuffer prefix rule.
Skipped-unless-built smoke test of the published lib/index.js path, importing the package by name through its exports map.
Pins framing, byte caps, invalid UTF-8, oversized writes, blocked-write settlement and that a channel-closing receiver raises no failure.
Pins the per-call/persistent-in-memory switch: programFormat flip, rejection of unsupported mode strings, and state discarded on a provider reload.
The largest host-failure matrix: config rejection, sandbox classification by runner evidence, protocol violations, cancellation races, output limits and environment scrubbing.
Differential test against the canonical snapshotJsonValue plus an adversarial container zoo (Map, subclasses, sparse, spoofed and revoked prototypes) and a 5000-deep round trip.
Pins launch selection and bootstrap mapping, including an explicit remote bootstrap used verbatim and the packaged-host default.
Pins exact byte accounting against JSON.stringify's own length and proves the measurement is unchanged after eight JavaScript intrinsics are mutated.
Pins the combined output cap at four budgets and the rule that an oversized diagnostic is replaced rather than truncated.
Pins drain semantics: already-ended returns true, destroyed returns false, and a retained descriptor is bounded by the grace timer.
Skipped-unless-built smoke test of the retained mode through lib/index.js plus lib/persistent-process.js, including the release that drops the state.
Host-side failure matrix for the retained mode: three policy-change races, protocol violations, the cleanup barrier that blocks reuse, and idle-crash cleanup tracking.
Exercises the child REPL over an in-memory channel: injected process isolation, per-evaluation output attribution, leading-brace blocks and completed-evaluation refusals.
Pins the retained mode's file policy: retained variables under read-only, a one-shot escalation that sees no standing variables, fail-closed confinement and policy-change invalidation.
The behavioural spec of the retained REPL: what survives across evaluations, what is destroyed by a timeout, current-binding dispatch, and release semantics.
Pins the policy-invalidation bookkeeping: cleanup without a new execution, a failed cleanup retried, temporary-escalation separation and disposal joining.
Pins the per-call child's handshake, null-prototype environment scrub, late-reply tolerance and exit-code semantics after a malformed frame.
Boots the unbuilt source closure outside the workspace over a real inherited fd 7 socket, proving the bootstrap has no sibling built exports.
End-to-end per-call behaviour against a real Node process and a real local sandbox: empty env, nested processes, deadlines, heap cap, hostile fd-7 traffic and symlink escape.
Shared harness that mounts the local session/fs/subprocess/sandbox providers and the Node PTC runtime into a fresh Context.
Project reference for the Node backend, listing the session, timeout, fs, subprocess, sandbox, sandbox-policy and ptc-runtime projects it compiles against.
Three-bundle tsdown config; the two child bundles inline dsh-subprocess/control with noExternal because a remote host cannot resolve a workspace package.
Published manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime; no runtime dependencies at all, only cordis and dsh-sandbox peers.
Heading-hash record pairing the seam README's English and Chinese, 18 sections including the Dev Note.
Package reference for the abstract seam: resolve/run, the portable identifier rules, the eight failure kinds and the stated limitations.
Chinese mirror of the seam README; its limitations section states the same limits as current contract rather than a backlog.
The Service Definition: the abstract PtcRuntime service plus the four shared portable-identifier exclusion sets, each with a stated reason.
The seam's whole vocabulary, including the orthogonal eight-kind failure taxonomy and the rule that a failure is a field on a resolved result.
Pins the shared exclusion sets' membership, including that __ and ____ are not dunder forms and that lambda is refused for portability.
Exercises the abstract seam through a StubRuntime: registration, error-as-field, pre-aborted signal, HMR disposal and duplicate-service rejection.
Project reference for the seam package, referencing cosmokit, cordis and the sandbox project.
Heading-hash record for the PTC package-group README, 5 sections.
Package-group map naming the three PTC packages and which one owns the ctx.ptcRuntime key and the fd-3 Python wire.
Chinese mirror of the PTC package-group map.
Published manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-ssh; zod is pinned exactly at 4.4.3 because the remote wire schemas are a compatibility surface.
Heading-hash record pairing the fs-ssh README's English and Chinese, 9 sections.
Package reference for the remote filesystem provider: no configuration fields, undefined processPathFromHostPath, 8 MiB transfer caps and no watch.
Chinese mirror of the fs-ssh README; states the no-auto-retry rule as a semantic guarantee.
Remote ctx.fs: every operation is one schema-validated ssh.request; contains() uses posix.relative so a sibling prefix is not inside, and error codes are mapped by a whitelist.
Pins the remote filesystem provider against a fake connection that parses with the real schemas: file URLs, containment, error codes, cancellation and stream closing.
Project reference for fs-ssh, referencing cordis, schemastery, the ssh package, fs, sandbox and sandbox-policy.
Heading-hash record for the SSH group README, 5 sections including the Dev Note's path invariant.
Package-group map for the POSIX SSH family: four services across five packages, and the rule that local access must never be inferred from a remote path string.
Chinese mirror of the SSH group README, stating the path invariant as an absolute rule.
Published manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-ssh; it does not peer-depend on sandbox-policy because the policy is passed per call.
Heading-hash record pairing the sandbox-ssh README's English and Chinese, 9 sections.
Package reference for the remote sandbox provider: the remote host selects its own backend, and the SSH host and helper are trusted infrastructure.
Chinese mirror of the sandbox-ssh README, keeping the trusted-infrastructure caveat.
Remote ctx.sandbox: confines argv on the far host over a strict facts schema; every failure becomes a SandboxUnavailableError and cancellation is checked before and after.
Pins the remote confinement provider: it awaits the remote answer, rejects malformed facts before exposing argv, and sends a failed request exactly once.
Project reference for sandbox-ssh, referencing one project fewer than fs-ssh because it needs no sandbox-policy.
Private manifest for the helper runtime; its dependency list is the authoritative spec of what the pkg --sea binary embeds.
Heading-hash record pairing the helper-runtime README's English and Chinese, 10 sections.
Build, verify, install and publish guide for the self-contained helper executable: four native targets, a digest manifest and two verifier lanes.
Chinese mirror of the helper-runtime README, same targets and glibc 2.28 baseline.
SEA dispatcher for the packaged binary: a module-resolution hook redirects the native package to the co-shipped directory, and both selector env vars are deleted before dispatch.
Loader-mounted fixture that talks to a real helper executable over local sockets using the production SshRpcPeer, helloSchema and authenticateStream.
Artifact-verification driver: a real Loader composition exercising files, processes, cancellation, native PTY, embedded PTC, native flock and the sandbox lanes.
AlmaLinux 8.10 image (glibc 2.28) with openssh-server and no Node, for the SSH portability lane.
Key-only, PAM-free sshd configuration with Unix-socket forwarding enabled and VERBOSE logging.
Container entrypoint that generates a per-run host key, installs the disposable public key and execs sshd in the foreground.
Project reference for the helper runtime, listing exactly the four modules the SEA dispatcher can import.
Published manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-ssh; ./protocol and ./schemas are public exports so sibling providers share the wire without reaching into src.
Heading-hash record pairing the SSH package README's English and Chinese, 8 sections.
Package reference for the SSH connection: deployment prerequisites, the config table, per-stream TLS-PSK isolation, and the never-replay rule.
Chinese mirror of the SSH package README; keeps the SIGUSR1 hardening as its own paragraph.
OpenSSH-side helper entry: accepts no command arguments, aborts the transport on TERM/HUP/INT, and reports every failure on stderr with exit code 127.
Remote process ownership: prepare-then-start reservations, per-channel TLS endpoints, the 30-second reservation expiry, the collected-output forwarder and cleanup that joins native quiescence.
The remote helper: serves the administrative RPC by delegating to the local providers installed beside it, with a client lease, a one-shot handshake and bounded text iterators.
The OpenSSH connection owner: hardened non-interactive ssh argv, digest/kind/bootstrap verification before readiness, heartbeat lease, per-stream forwarding and SIGUSR1 disabled.
The bounded versioned RPC: reserved capacity per request class, cancellation that keeps the credit until the far side replies, and a never-replay rule.
Strict zod schemas for every request and observation, with branded UUID identities, a remotePath rule and a null environment tombstone.
TLS-PSK authentication for forwarded streams: pinned cipher and TLS version, no unauthenticated fallback, a handshake deadline, and a paused returned socket.
Pins the collected-output contract: the bounded tail and the whole-stream totalBytes reported separately, and the spill file surviving helper shutdown.
Pins client disposal ordering: requests refused without being sent, a heartbeat still admitted under ordinary load, control commands force-killed and joined, and listener removal.
Shared harness serving a real helper over an in-memory transport, reusing the production SshRpcPeer and authenticateStream, with a realpath'd root.
Pins lease expiry, the double-checked text-stream capacity, the 8 MiB transfer bounds, iterator cancellation and cleanup failure surfacing through the serving lifetime.
Proves helper shutdown joins a completed process's directory removal rather than racing it, and that a late done returns the identical outcome object.
Proves a failed native launch releases the single-process capacity while the original error object is preserved for later done reads.
Proves an authenticated TLS fault destroys the native control endpoint and that a release still observing the range keeps ownership of the completion.
Pins reservation ownership: capacity reserved before the async allocation, a close during prepare rejecting it, and a termination that prevents the process from ever being published.
The remote process settlement matrix: terminal operations, a bounded completed-result cache, fd-7 absence, socket-path length limits, live snapshots and native cleanup failures.
Pins the helper's real behaviour over the wire: no chdir, guarded writes, symlink identity, text iterator closure, unconfined sandbox refusal and name-based error-code mapping.
Pins the branded identity types: SshProcessId and SshTextStreamId are not assignable to each other even though the wire value is one UUID.
Proves a same-user sandboxed process can attach a Node inspector unless --disable-sigusr1 is set; the probe runs both ways and asserts the difference.
Opt-in acceptance against a real disposable SSH host: a same-user TLS attacker, fd-7 binary round trip, control progress while stdout is paused, and disconnect cleanup.
Proves each request class has its own capacity so heartbeat and close stay available under a full ordinary load, and that cancellation keeps the credit.
Pins the protocol's framing, queueing and inbound admission: zero-byte rejection before transmission, reentrant close, fragmented chunks and refused inbound requests.
Proves queued requests settle after a peer close, output close or input EOF even with no drain event, and that no listeners are left behind.
Small high-level protocol spec: typed remote errors, response schema failures, cancellation without replay, and an unknown outcome after a disconnect.
The client startup matrix: eleven invalid configs refused before spawn, identity verification, quoted remote commands, cancellation races, forwarding and disposal.
Pins the per-stream capability: a wrong TLS identity is refused without consuming the reservation, only one client is published, and forged admin bytes are opaque.
Pins cancellation ownership after TLS takes over the socket, including a primitive abort reason propagated verbatim.
Adversarial test: a confined process renames the socket and relays the TLS bytes, and still learns neither the plaintext nor the capability key.
Pins the TLS authentication deadline: a peer that accepts the connection but never handshakes is closed after 25 ms.
Project reference for the SSH package, listing exactly the providers the helper mounts in its private Context.
Single tsdown pass producing four bundles, with helper bundled separately because the remote host runs it with no workspace to resolve from.
Published manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-ssh; it peer-depends on subprocess-local to reuse the same OutputCollector client-side.
Heading-hash record pairing the subprocess-ssh README's English and Chinese, 9 sections.
Package reference for the remote subprocess provider: the handle is usable before allocation, done and waitForExit are different facts, and ambiguous work is never replayed.
Chinese mirror of the subprocess-ssh README, keeping the done-versus-waitForExit distinction explicit.
Remote ctx.subprocess: RemoteProcess and the provider, absolute collected-output offsets with rewind rejection, and disposal that raises when cleanup cannot be confirmed.
Proves the provider joins an unpublished terminal allocation before disposal completes and still sends process.terminate for a reservation whose stream was never opened.
The ordinary-process contract: inherit mode without ending host streams, independent channels, absolute offsets, snapshot rejection, at most one termination, and refusals after disposal.
Pins the remote shell facts and the code-based (not class-based) distinction between a lookup miss and a transport failure, plus a real-helper PTY resize.
Pins caller-owned stream closure and the bounded range observation across every stage, including abort-listener detachment and the real failure preserved.
Pins the terminal contract: memoised termination, retry after a cleanup failure, a failed done still terminable, and both errors reported when allocation and cleanup both fail.
Project reference for subprocess-ssh, referencing subprocess-local for the OutputCollector import rather than for local execution.
